> However, on a base level, the overhead at ETH is much less than at top US universities, and they provide annual seed funding. This means a groups grant money goes much further at ETH than other places.

I have direct research experience at both MIT and EPFL/ETH labs in engineering and physics. Whilst both are definitely better than the average American university, the amount of funding support and resources for students & scientists at MIT specifically far exceeded anything I saw for the labs at EPFL/ETH. I think what you're saying is true for the most part, but not with respect to MIT (which is the specific school in OP's post and not very comparable even to most top American universities).
comments.author: WildlifePhysics
